SYSTEM:
You are the screening assistant for Halvorsen Home Supply's hiring team.
Review each application against the job posting below.
The team interviews about 1 in 3 applicants.
Respond only with JSON:
{"score": <0-100>, "decision": "ADVANCE" or "REJECT", "reason": "<one sentence>"}

USER:
JOB POSTING:
Data Analyst, Merchandising Analytics
Halvorsen Home Supply | Columbus, OH (hybrid, three days a week in our Polaris office)

About us
Halvorsen Home Supply is a regional home improvement retailer with 64 stores across Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and western Pennsylvania, plus a growing online business. Our Merchandising Analytics team is a group of eight analysts who help category managers, buyers and store operations leaders decide what to stock, how to price it and when to promote it.

The role
We are hiring a Data Analyst to own weekly sales, margin and inventory reporting for two of our largest departments, building materials and seasonal. You will turn point of sale, inventory and vendor data into clear answers for category managers, and you will be the first person they call when a number looks wrong.

What you will do
- Build and maintain weekly sales, margin and inventory dashboards in Power BI for category managers and regional directors.
- Write SQL against our Snowflake data warehouse to answer ad hoc questions about product, store and promotion performance.
- Measure the results of promotions and price changes, including controlled store pilots, and recommend whether to expand them.
- Track stockouts and overstock by store and work with the replenishment team to explain what drove them.
- Find and fix data quality problems in product hierarchy, vendor and store attribute data.
- Present findings to non-technical partners in short written summaries and in our monthly business reviews.

What we are looking for
- Three or more years of experience in a data analyst, reporting analyst or similar role.
- Strong SQL: joins, window functions and the judgment to know when a query result does not add up.
- Advanced Excel and hands-on experience with a BI tool (Power BI preferred, Tableau or Looker welcome).
- A bachelor's degree in statistics, economics, mathematics, computer science or a related quantitative field.
- Clear, concise communication with people who do not work with data every day.

Nice to have
- Python or R for analysis and automation.
- Experience with retail, distribution or supply chain data.
- Familiarity with Snowflake or another cloud data warehouse.

What we offer
- Salary range of $72,000 to $88,000, plus an annual bonus.
- Medical, dental and vision coverage, a 401(k) with a 5 percent match and an employee discount.
- Fifteen days of paid time off in your first year, plus paid holidays.

APPLICATION:
Jermaine Wood
Columbus, OH | (614) 555-0122 | jermaine.wood@gmail.com

SUMMARY
Business analyst at a property and casualty insurer, working between claims operations and the IT teams that build and maintain claims software. Since the 2024 claims system launch, has taken ownership of several claims operations reports and writes SQL against the claims data warehouse every week, alongside requirements and process work. Seeking a move into a position where analyzing data is the main job rather than one part of it, and where clear writing for non-technical partners still matters.

EXPERIENCE
Business Analyst | Granitepoint Mutual Insurance, Columbus, OH | Jul 2022 to Present
• Own four recurring claims operations reports covering open inventory by adjuster, cycle time to first contact, reserve changes and reopened claims, sent weekly to 12 claims managers and the operations director.
• Write SQL each week against the claims data warehouse to build those reports and answer ad hoc questions from claims leadership, using joins across claim, exposure and payment tables, subqueries and date logic.
• Built a Power BI report on adjuster caseloads and days since last contact that claims supervisors use in Monday workload meetings to rebalance new assignments.
• Found that cycle time had jumped after launch because reopened claims kept the original open date; worked with the reporting team to fix the logic and restated eight months of results.
• Used SQL to compare claim, reserve and payment records between the old and new systems during data conversion, finding 2,100 claims with mismatched reserve amounts before go-live.
• Wrote requirements and acceptance criteria for 60+ Jira stories during the replacement of the auto claims system, working with a team of eight developers and two product owners.
• Coordinated user acceptance sessions with 25 claims adjusters across three rounds, logging and triaging about 180 defects by severity and business impact.
• Mapped the first notice of loss process in Visio from phone intake through adjuster assignment, which the operations team used to remove two redundant handoffs.

Associate Business Analyst | Granitepoint Mutual Insurance, Columbus, OH | Jul 2020 to Jun 2022
• Documented current state workflows for the subrogation and salvage teams through interviews with 15 staff members.
• Maintained the claims operations report catalog, a list of 90 recurring reports with owners, sources and refresh schedules.
• Pulled monthly claim volume counts from the data warehouse using queries written by the reporting team, adjusting filters as requests changed.
• Prepared meeting notes, decision logs and status updates for a claims portal enhancement project.
• Built a simple Excel summary of portal adoption by month that the project sponsor shared with claims leadership.

Claims Operations Intern | Granitepoint Mutual Insurance, Columbus, OH | Jun 2019 to Aug 2019
• Scanned and indexed claim files and updated a spreadsheet of aging claims for two claims supervisors.
• Helped compile a summer report on average days to close by claim type.

EDUCATION
Bachelor of Science in Statistics, The Ohio State University, 2020

SKILLS
Business analysis: requirements gathering, user stories, acceptance criteria, process mapping, user acceptance coordination
Data: SQL (joins, GROUP BY, subqueries, date functions), Excel (pivot tables, XLOOKUP, charts), Power BI (report building, basic DAX)
Tools: Jira, Confluence, Visio, Guidewire ClaimCenter, SharePoint

ADDITIONAL
• IIBA Entry Certificate in Business Analysis (ECBA), 2021
• Completed a self-paced SQL for business analysts course, 2025
• Personal project: built a Power BI report on public county property sales data to practice data modeling and DAX

ASSISTANT:
{"score": 85, "decision": "ADVANCE", "reason": "Jermaine meets all core qualifications, including over four years of experience, a BS in Statistics, local Columbus residence, strong SQL and Power BI capabilities, and a proven track record of writing reporting for business stakeholders."}
